entries.name: Floor Straddle Planche Hold

source.provenance: Losslessly encoded original human excerpt at unchanged dimensions and cadence; audio omitted. No generated, composited or reversed frames.

entries.basis: The fixed straight-elbow, straight-knee straddle planche holds the trunk horizontally without foot or external support. Its shortened wide-leg lever sits between the existing tucked tier-3 and straight-joined-leg tier-5 planches: provisional NM strength tier 4. Horizontal two-palm equilibrium supports task-specific balance tier 3. The exact hold, not an easier tucked version or a full joined-leg planche, is prescribed.
entries.trainingConditions: Use clean brief attempts or repetitions with deliberate recovery inside the 45-second opportunity. Retain the demonstrated floor support, limb position and complete action. No sustained 45-second maximum, repetition count, endurance tier, ballistic power, cardio capacity or measured performance is inferred. These are provisional NM task categories, not externally validated physiological cutoffs.
entries.equipment: Feet, hands and a brief setup knee contact require Floor and exclude Hard Floor. No bars, bands, elevation or wall. Ordinary shoes are compatible; controlled execution is quiet. Static planche excludes Insect; moving push-ups permit it.
entries.identity: Different fixed mechanics; neither is an alias of a tucked static planche or a straight joined-leg full planche.

entries.name: Floor Tuck Planche Push-Ups

source.provenance: Losslessly encoded original human excerpt at unchanged dimensions and cadence; audio omitted. No generated, composited or reversed frames.

entries.basis: The fixed unsupported tucked push-up lowers and raises the whole body through elbow flexion/extension while both feet remain airborne and the knees do not rest on the upper arms. This adds a complete loaded pressing cycle to the existing tier-3 static tuck planche, supporting provisional strength tier 4; equilibrium and coordinated reversal remain tier 3. The full straight-body floor 90-degree press remains a distinct tier-5 task.
